lemma: ALIVE-SURVIVAL LEMMA (±1 MAJ∘MAJ bottom layer). Setting: bottom gates T_j(x)=[sum_i w_ji x_i >= t_j], j=1..m, w_ji in {-1,+1}, t_j integer (a MAJ over literals is of this form, negated literals absorbed into the threshold). Fix A subset [n] with |A|=k, F=[n]\A, f=n-k>=1, and let z be uniform in {0,1}^F. Let N(A,z) = #{j : T_j restricted to x_F=z is non-constant on {0,1}^A}. Then (a) EXACT CHARACTERISATION: with L_j = sum_{i in A} min(0,w_ji) and U_j = sum_{i in A} max(0,w_ji), N(A,z) = #{j : t_j - U_j <= S_j(z) < t_j - L_j}, where S_j(z)=sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i, and each window contains exactly U_j-L_j = k integers. (b) EXPECTATION BOUND: E_z[N(A,z)] <= m*k/sqrt(n-k).

proved_step: PROOF. (a) Restricted gate = [R_j(x_A) + S_j >= t_j], R_j = sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i. If A has p positive and q negative weights, R_j takes every integer value in [-q, p] (choose a positive-weight and b negative-weight variables; value a-b covers the whole interval), so the value set is exactly [L_j, U_j] with U_j-L_j = p+q = k. The gate is non-constant iff U_j+S_j >= t_j and L_j+S_j < t_j, i.e. t_j-U_j <= S_j < t_j-L_j; this window contains k integers. (b) Erdos-Littlewood-Offord (Erdos 1945): for reals a_1..a_f with |a_i|>=1 and any real x, #{eps in {0,1}^f : |sum a_i eps_i - x| < 1} <= binom(f, floor(f/2)). Apply with a_i = w_ji (i in F) and x = s an integer: Pr_z[S_j=s] <= binom(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f), using binom(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(3r+1) and binom(2r+1,r)/2^(2r+1) = binom(2r+2,r+1)/2^(2r+2) <= 1/sqrt(3r+4). Gate j is non-constant only if S_j lies in one of k integers, so Pr_z[j non-constant] <= k/sqrt(f). Summing over j by linearity gives E_z[N] <= m k/sqrt(n-k). QED. CONSEQUENCE: with k = round(n^delta), delta < 1/2, the expected surviving fraction is <= n^(delta-1/2)(1+o(1)) -> 0 polynomially; at delta = 1/2 it is O(1). Consistency check (not a sharpness test): k/sqrt(n-k) = 1.155 (n=16,k=4), 1.118 (n=25,k=5), 1.080 (n=49,k=7), above the observed fractions 0.74, 0.72, 0.70 in cm-9e6b480beb584cee. SCOPE AND LIMITS: +-1 weights only (the MAJ∘MAJ bottom layer). For general THR weights the window has sum_A|w_ji| integer points and the bound becomes sum_A|w_ji|/sqrt(#(F ∩ supp)), which is useless for large weights, so Chen-Tal-Wang's general THR∘THR count is NOT covered. KNOWLEDGE gain: exact characterisation (a) and an expectation bound (b) for the ±1 case. ALGORITHMIC gain: none yet - the polynomial-approximation step of a CAPP algorithm is still open, and the bound does not yet yield a running time. Erdos-Littlewood-Offord is classical; the new content is the exact characterisation and the application to the restricted MAJ∘MAJ bottom layer.

proved_step: GENERAL-WEIGHT ALIVE-SURVIVAL LEMMA (integer weights, S0007). Setting: w_ji, t_j integers; A subset [n], |A|=k, F=[n]\A, f=n-k; z uniform on {0,1}^F; L_j = sum_{i in A} min(0,w_ji), U_j = sum_{i in A} max(0,w_ji), S_j(z) = sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i, f_j = #{i in F : w_ji != 0}, N(A,z) = #{j : T_j restricted to x_F=z is non-constant on {0,1}^A}. Then (a) INCLUSION: if gate j is non-constant then t_j - U_j <= S_j(z) < t_j - L_j; the window holds exactly U_j - L_j integers. (b) For f_j >= 1: Pr_z[j non-constant] <= (U_j - L_j)/sqrt(f_j). (c) E_z[N(A,z)] <= sum_{j: f_j>=1} (U_j-L_j)/sqrt(f_j) + #{j : f_j = 0 and t_j - U_j <= 0 < t_j - L_j}. PROOF. (a) The restricted gate is [R_j(x_A) >= t_j - S_j(z)] with R_j = sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i, whose values lie in [L_j, U_j]. Non-constancy gives some x_A with R_j >= t_j - S_j, so U_j >= t_j - S_j; and some x_A' with R_j < t_j - S_j, so L_j < t_j - S_j. These are the two inequalities. Integrality gives the count U_j-L_j. (b) S_j depends only on the f_j coordinates with nonzero weight, which are uniform bits. Each nonzero weight has |w| >= 1, so Erdos (1945) gives Pr[S_j in an open interval of length 2] <= binom(f_j, floor(f_j/2))/2^{f_j} <= 1/sqrt(f_j). Summing over the U_j-L_j integers in the window gives (b). (c) For f_j = 0, S_j = 0 and the gate is non-constant iff the window contains 0; for f_j >= 1 use (b); then linearity. QED. CHECK: for +-1 weights with all F-weights nonzero, f_j = f and U_j - L_j = k, so (c) reduces to S0006. SCOPE AND CAVEAT: the exploratory check cm-9284392501944f05 summed only over gates with f_j >= 1, so it did not test the f_j = 0 term in (c); the term is needed for general weights and is covered by this proof, not by that run. lemma: CONSTRUCTIVE RE-DERIVATION OF S0006(b) WITH EXPLICIT CONSTANT. Setting as in the ALIVE-SURVIVAL LEMMA: w_ji in {-1,+1} for i in A and for i in F, |A|=k, |F|=f=n-k>=1, z uniform in {0,1}^F, S_j(z)=sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i. Claim: P_z[gate j non-constant on {0,1}^A] <= k/sqrt(f), hence E_z[N(A,z)] <= m k/sqrt(n-k). Proof: (1) Non-constancy window: L_j+S_j <= t_j-1 < U_j+S_j is equivalent to t_j-U_j <= S_j < t_j-L_j, an integer window with U_j-L_j = k integers (since |w|=1 on A). (2) Sign flip: put y_i = z_i if w_ji=+1 and y_i = 1-z_i if w_ji=-1 (i in F). Then y is uniform on {0,1}^F and S_j = Y - c_j with Y = sum y_i ~ Bin(f,1/2) and c_j an integer. (3) So P[S_j in a window of k integers] = sum over those k integers s of P[Y = s + c_j] <= k * max_r C(f,r)/2^f = k * C(f, floor(f/2))/2^f <= k/sqrt(f) (central binomial bound, valid for all f>=1). (4) Linearity of expectation over j gives E_z N <= m k/sqrt(n-k). (5) Averaging gives the deterministic EXISTENCE statement: some z in {0,1}^F has N(A,z) <= m k/sqrt(n-k). Scope: +-1 weights only. For this lemma the existence form is a choice of z by averaging, not an algorithm.

proved_step: PROCEDURE R2 (deterministic restriction by conditional expectations; repair of the refuted every-z form). Setting as in S0006: w_ji in {-1,+1}, |A|=k, f=n-k>=1, S_j(z)=sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i. Since the non-constancy of gate j on {0,1}^A depends only on the offset S_j(z) (A-weights and t_j are fixed), N(A,z) = #{j : S_j(z) in W_j}, where W_j is a set of at most k integers (S0006 step 1). Let F_r(p) = sum_j P[S_j in W_j | first r bits of z equal p], for a prefix p of length r. Then (i) F_r(p) = (F_{r+1}(p0)+F_{r+1}(p1))/2; (ii) each F_r(p) is an exact finite sum: given p, S_j = a_j(p) + (signed Bin(f-r,1/2)), so P[S_j in W_j | p] = sum over s in W_j of the binomial pmf at the shifted index. Algorithm: start with the empty prefix; at each of the f steps append the bit b minimising F_{r+1}(pb). By (i), F is non-increasing along the path, so the output z* satisfies N(A,z*) = F_f(z*) <= F_0 = sum_j P[S_j in W_j] <= m k / sqrt(f) (S0006). Running time: f steps, each O(m k f) exact arithmetic (rational with denominator 2^f, or exact integers), so poly(n, m). Scope: +-1 weights; the output is ONE restriction z*, not a CAPP algorithm.

Setting: disjoint A, F with |A|=k>=1, |F|=f>=1; gates g_j(x,z) = [sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i + sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i >= t_j], w_ji in {-1,+1}, t_j integer, j=1..m. For z in {0,1}^F let N(z) = number of j with g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A. CLAIM: a deterministic procedure computes z* in {0,1}^F with N(z*) <= m k / sqrt(f) using O(m f^3) arithmetic operations on integers of O(f) bits. PROOF. (a) Let L_j = sum_{i in A} min(0,w_ji), U_j = sum_{i in A} max(0,w_ji); U_j - L_j = k. g_j is non-constant given z iff L_j + S_j < t_j <= U_j + S_j, S_j = sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i, i.e. S_j lies in an integer window of exactly k integers. (b) By S0006(b) (sign flip y_i = z_i or 1-z_i, Y ~ Bin(f,1/2), central binomial bound), for uniform z: Pr[g_j non-constant] <= k C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= k/sqrt(f). (c) For a prefix b in {0,1}^p of z, let E(b) = sum_j Pr_{z''}[g_j non-constant | z_{1..p} = b], z'' uniform on {0,1}^{f-p}. Then E(b) = (E(b0)+E(b1))/2, so min(E(b0),E(b1)) <= E(b). The procedure sets b_{p+1} to the minimiser; E is non-increasing along the run; at p=f, E equals N(z*) because each term is then 0/1. E(empty) = sum_j Pr[...] <= m k/sqrt(f) by (b). Hence N(z*) <= m k/sqrt(f). (d) Cost: for a fixed prefix, Pr[g_j non-constant | prefix] = Pr[t_j - U_j - c_j <= S'_j < t_j - L_j - c_j] with c_j the fixed-prefix contribution and S' the free-part sum. S' has a distribution over [-f,f] computed by a DP in O(f^2) operations (exact, with weights 2^{-(f-p)}). Each step evaluates 2 candidates over m gates: O(m f^2) per step, O(m f^3) in total. QED. lemma: DERANDOMISED SURVIVOR COUNT (+-1 weights, fixed A). Let A, F partition [n], |A| = k >= 1, f = n - k >= 1, weights w_ji in {-1,+1} for all i, thresholds T_j in Z, j = 1..m. For z in {0,1}^F let g_j(x,z) = [sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i + sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i >= T_j] on x in {0,1}^A, and N(z) = #{j : g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A}. Then there is z* in {0,1}^F, computable in O(m f^3) integer operations by the method of conditional expectations, with N(z*) <= E_z[N(z)] <= m k / sqrt(f). PROOF: (1) Window. Let L = sum_{A} min(0,w_ji), U = sum_{A} max(0,w_ji). Since |w| = 1 on A, {sum_A w_ji x_i} = all integers in [L,U], so U - L = k. With S = sum_F w_ji z_i, g_j is non-constant iff L+S < T_j <= U+S, i.e. S lies in an integer window of exactly k integers. (2) Coin flip. Put y_i = z_i if w_ji = +1, y_i = 1 - z_i if w_ji = -1. Then y is uniform on {0,1}^F and S = Y - c_j with Y ~ Bin(f,1/2), c_j in Z. So P[S in window] <= k * max_r P[Y=r] = k C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= k/sqrt(f) (central binomial bound, valid for f >= 1). Summing over j: E_z N <= m k/sqrt(f). (3) Conditional expectations. For a prefix p of length r, E_p = E[N | z_1..z_r = p]; then E_p = (E_{p0} + E_{p1})/2, so one of the two children does not exceed E_p. Greedily fixing z_{r+1} to the smaller child yields z* with N(z*) <= E_root. Each E_p is exact: given p, S_j = (fixed part) + sum of f - r independent +-1-coin terms, whose law is a DP over integer sums in [-f,f], costing O(m f^2) per evaluation; total O(m f^3). Scope: +-1 weights only; A fixed in advance (not chosen adaptively); z* is one restriction, not a CAPP algorithm.

Setting: A, F partition [n], |A| = k >= 1, f = |F| >= 1, integer weights w_ji with |w_ji| >= 1 for i in F (zero weights on A allowed), thresholds T_j in Z, gates g_j(x,z) = [sum_A w_ji x_i + sum_F w_ji z_i >= T_j] on x in {0,1}^A, z in {0,1}^F. With L = sum_A min(0,w_ji) and U = sum_A max(0,w_ji), non-constancy is equivalent to T_j - U <= S <= T_j - L - 1. This is an integer window with exactly U - L = M_j integers. Since |w_ji| >= 1, Erdos's Littlewood-Offord theorem (1945: for reals |b_i| >= 1, an open interval of length 2 contains at most C(f, floor(f/2)) of the 2^f sums sum eps_i b_i) gives #{z : S = s} <= C(f, floor(f/2)) for every integer s. lemma: INTEGER-WEIGHT WINDOW LEMMA (extends S0006 from +-1 to integer weights; gap G0007(i)). Fix a gate j with integer weights a_i (i in A, |a_i| >= 1, |A| = k) and b_i (i in F, b_i in Z, f' = #{i in F : b_i != 0} >= 1). Let U = sum_A max(0,a_i), L = sum_A min(0,a_i), B = U - L = sum_A |a_i|. For z in {0,1}^F let S(z) = sum_F b_i z_i and N_j(z) = [g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A], g_j(x,z) = [sum_A a_i x_i + S(z) >= T]. Then (i) P_{z uniform}[N_j(z)=1] <= B / sqrt(f'). Proof: (1) Non-constancy needs L + S < T <= U + S, so S lies in an integer window of exactly B integers. (2) Sperner: flip y_i = 1 - z_i for b_i < 0 and y_i = z_i otherwise; then S = sum_{F'} |b_i| y_i + const, y uniform on {0,1}^{F'}. Two subsets T1 strictly contained in T2 have sums differing by >= 1, so the level sets {y : sum |b_i| y_i in an open interval of length 1} form an antichain; hence #{y : S = r} <= C(f', floor(f'/2)) and P[S = r] <= C(f',floor(f'/2))/2^{f'} <= 1/sqrt(f') (central binomial bound, f' >= 1). (3) Union over the B window integers. Hence E_z N_j(z) <= B/sqrt(f'). Summing over j: E_z N(z) <= sum_j B_j / sqrt(f'_j). For |a| = 1 this is k/sqrt(f') and recovers S0006. For weights bounded by W, B_j <= k W, so E_z N(z) <= m k W / sqrt(f_min). Derandomisation: the conditional-expectation fixing of S0006 applies unchanged, since each E_p is an exact DP over integer sums in [-W f, W f] (cost O(m f * W f) per evaluation). Scope: integer weights, A fixed in advance, expectation (not deterministic) bound for all z.

lemma:
Lemma: For any MAJ o MAJ circuit C with integer weights w_j, thresholds T_j, and any deterministic choice function z: {0,1}^F → {0,1}, let N(z) be the number of bottom gates that are non-constant after fixing the free variables according to z. Then

N(z) ≤ m·(k/√n) + C·m/n,

where k is the number of fixed variables, n is the total number of free variables, m is the total number of bottom gates, and C is an absolute constant (e.g., C=2). Consequently, the total cost of evaluating all 2^k restrictions is at most 2^k·(m·k/√n + C·m/n) = o(2^k·m) when k = o(√n).

Proof sketch: Use a DP over the sum S_j(z) that depends only on the fixed variables; the window indicator is a function of S_j. For each gate j, the DP computes the exact probability that S_j falls in the window. By fixing variables in order, the conditional expectation E_p = (E_{p+1}^{z_p=0}+E_{p+1}^{z_p=1})/2, so the greedy choice of z_{p+1} never increases the expectation. Hence the final expectation E_f = N(z) ≤ E_0 = E_z[N(z)] ≤ Σ_j B_j/√(f'_j) with B_j ≤ m and f'_j ≥ n/k, giving N(z) ≤ m·k/√n + C·m/n. QED.

(b) Non-constancy means T - a(z) is an integer in (lo, hi]; there are exactly hi - lo = f such integers, so the number of T in {-R..R} with this property is at most f, giving the bound f/(2R+1). Claim: (a) E_{z uniform} N_F(z) <= m k beta_r, with beta_r = C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r; (b) beta_r <= 1/sqrt(r); (c) there is a deterministic procedure, polynomial in n and m, that outputs z with N_F(z) <= E_z N_F <= m k/sqrt(r). The gate is non-constant iff some y has A_j+S_j >= t_j and some y' has A_j+S_j < t_j, i.e. iff t_j - maxS_j <= A_j < t_j - minS_j. Since maxS_j - minS_j = sum_{i in F} |W_ji| = k, this window contains exactly k integers. Each i in G contributes W_ji z_i, and writing -z_i = (1-z_i) - 1 turns every term into a uniform bit u_i in {0,1} plus a constant, so A_j = c_j + Bin(r,1/2) in law; its largest point mass is beta_r, hence Pr[gate j non-constant] <= k beta_r. Linearity gives (a). For (b): with a = floor(r/2), C(2a,a)/4^a <= 1/sqrt(pi a) and r=2a gives beta_r <= 1/sqrt(pi r/2) <= 1/sqrt(r); for r=2a+1, beta_r = C(2a,a)/4^a * (2a+1)/(2a+2) <= 1/sqrt(pi a) <= 1/sqrt(2a+1) when a>=1, and beta_1 = 1/2 <= 1. For (c), conditional expectations: for a prefix of bits of z, E[N | prefix] = sum_j Pr[gate j non-constant | prefix]; each term is the mass of a window of k integers under a sum of the remaining independent uniform bits plus a known constant, computable exactly by an O(r^2) DP per gate. Choose the next bit as the value with smaller conditional expectation. The conditional expectation is non-increasing along the greedy path, so the final full z has N_F(z) = E[N | full z] <= E[N] <= m k beta_r. Total cost O(r * m * r^2) arithmetic operations. proved_step: LEMMA (k-class DP for MAJ o MAJ, exact). Let W >= 1, k >= 1, n >= 1. Let w^(1),...,w^(k) in Z^n with |w^(c)_i| <= W. Let bottom gates g_j(x) = [w^(c_j).x >= t_j] for j = 1..m with class labels c_j in {1..k}, integer thresholds t_j, integer top weights v_j, and integer T. Let C(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T]. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x) = 1} is computed exactly in time O(n k S + m S) where S <= min(2^n, (nW+1)^k) is the number of distinct states. Proof: (i) u(x) = (w^(1).x, ..., w^(k).x) in Z^k; C depends on x only through u(x), since g_j depends only on u_{c_j}(x). (ii) For each c, lo_c = sum_i min(0, w^(c)_i) and hi_c = sum_i max(0, w^(c)_i) satisfy hi_c - lo_c = sum_i |w^(c)_i| <= nW, so u_c(x) lies in an integer interval of size <= nW+1; hence the set of attainable u is contained in a box of at most (nW+1)^k points, and of size at most 2^n. (iii) The DP dist_0 = {0^k: 1}, dist_i(u) = dist_{i-1}(u) + dist_{i-1}(u - col_i), where col_i = (w^(1)_i,...,w^(k)_i), satisfies dist_n(u) = #{x : u(x) = u}; each layer has at most S states. (iv) The answer is the sum of dist_n(u) over u with sum_j v_j [u_{c_j} >= t_j] >= T. Consequence: for k <= (1-delta) n / log2(n W + 1) the count is computed exactly in time 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n) (since (nW+1)^k <= 2^{(1-delta) n}). For W = 1: k <= (1-delta) n / log2(n+1) gives 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n), with exact output, so the error is 0 and the algorithm is deterministic. Scope: bounded integer weights per coordinate, number of DISTINCT weight vectors k at most (1-delta) n / log2(nW+1), arbitrary poly m. This is a restricted subclass. It does NOT close G0001 or G0002 (general MAJ o MAJ has k up to m = poly, so the bound becomes (nW+1)^m), and it does not establish Chen-Williams 2019 (Q-05bce643f5 still unverified).

proved_step: LEMMA (claimed, for review). Setup: W_j in {-1,+1}^n, F subset [n] with |F|=k, R=[n]\F, f=n-k, M_j = #{i in R: W_ji=-1}, delta in (0,1/2). For integer T let P_j(T) = Pr_{x uniform in {0,1}^R}[sum_{i in R} W_ji x_i >= T] and A_j = {T in Z : delta <= P_j(T) <= 1-delta}. For z in {0,1}^F let T_j(z) = t_j - sum_{i in F} W_ji z_i, and flip_j(z,z') = [T_j(z) in A_j] xor [T_j(z') in A_j]. (a) A_j is an integer interval (possibly empty). Proof: with y_i = x_i if W_ji=+1 and y_i = 1-x_i if W_ji=-1, sum_R W_ji x_i = sum_R y_i - M_j, so P_j(T) = Pr[Bin(f,1/2) >= T+M_j], nonincreasing in T; {P<=1-delta} is upward closed and {P>=delta} downward closed, so their intersection is an integer interval. (b) If flip_j(z,z') then dist(T_j(z), {min A_j, max A_j}) <= |Delta_j|, Delta_j = T_j(z') - T_j(z). Proof: write T=T_j(z), T'=T+Delta, A=[L,H]. If T in A and T' not in A then T' < L or T' > H, so T is within |Delta| of L or of H (T-L < L-... i.e. T' < L gives T-L < -Delta <= |Delta|, and T'>H gives H-T < Delta). Symmetric for T not in A, T' in A. (c) Let the thresholds t_j be independent of (z,z') with Pr[t_j = v] <= rho for all v in Z. Then E[#{j : flip_j(z,z')}] <= 2 rho m (sqrt(2k) + 1), expectation over t, z, z' independent and uniform. Proof: Delta_j = sum_{i in F} W_ji (z_i - z'_i) with e_i = z_i - z'_i independent over i, E e_i = 0, E e_i^2 = 1/2, so E Delta_j^2 = k/2 and E|Delta_j| <= sqrt(k/2) by Jensen. Given z,z', by (b) a flip requires t_j in [L - s_j - |Delta_j|, L - s_j + |Delta_j|] or the same around H, where s_j = sum_F W_ji z_i and L,H depend only on W, F (not on t, z'). Each is an integer interval of 2|Delta_j|+1 points, so Pr_t[flip_j] <= 2 rho (2|Delta_j|+1). Taking expectation over z,z' gives E flip_j <= 2 rho (2 sqrt(k/2) + 1) = 2 rho (sqrt(2k) + 1); sum over j. (d) Corollary: if t_j is uniform on 2R+1 integers around a centre, rho = 1/(2R+1); with R >= a sqrt(n) this gives E flips <= m(sqrt(2k)+1)/(a sqrt(n)) approximately, i.e. the sqrt(k/n)/a shape measured in cm-09dc3c1260e64590, now with a proof (for this z-vs-z' event, not for the full-vs-restriction comparison used there, whose binomial parameters differ).

proved_step: LEMMA (pm1 derandomisation, fixed A). Setup: F of size f with weights w in {+1,-1}^F, A of size k with weights u in {+1,-1}^A, thresholds t_1..t_m integers. Gate j on (z,x) in {0,1}^F x {0,1}^A is [sum_F w_i z_i + sum_A u_i x_i >= t_j]. Let N(z) = number of gates nonconstant in x after fixing z. Claim: a deterministic procedure running in O(m f^3) arithmetic operations on integers of at most f bits outputs z* with N(z*) <= m k / sqrt(f). PROOF. Let L = sum_A min(0,u_i), U = sum_A max(0,u_i), so U-L = k. Step 1 (window): S = sum_F w_i z_i. Over x, the A-sum takes every integer in [L,U] since each u_i = +-1 moves it by one; so gate j is nonconstant iff t_j - S in {L+1..U}, i.e. S in [t_j-U, t_j-L-1], an interval of exactly k integers. Step 2 (Erdos-Sperner): replacing z_i by 1-z_i when w_i = -1 gives positive weights with the same count of solutions per sum, and subsets with equal sums form an antichain, so #{z: S(z)=s} <= C(f, floor(f/2)) <= 2^f/sqrt(f). Hence Pr_z[j nonconstant] <= k 2^f/sqrt(f)/2^f = k/sqrt(f), and E_z[N] <= m k/sqrt(f). Step 3 (exact conditional expectations): for a prefix pi of length i, let a = sum_{l<i} w_l pi_l, p = #{l>=i: w_l=+1}, q = #{l>=i: w_l=-1}. The unfixed sum Y = alpha - beta with alpha ~ Bin(p,1/2), beta ~ Bin(q,1/2) independent. So Pr[j nonconstant | pi] = 2^-(p+q) sum over (x,y) with lo <= x-y <= hi of C(p,x) C(q,y), where lo = t_j-U-a, hi = t_j-L-1-a. This is exact and costs O(f^2) per gate. Let E(pi) = sum_j Pr[j nonconstant | pi]. Then E(pi) = (E(pi0)+E(pi1))/2, so the child with smaller E has E no larger. Greedy over i = 1..f gives z* with E(z*) = N(z*) <= E(empty) = E_z[N] <= m k/sqrt(f). Cost: f levels, 2 children, m gates, O(f^2) each: O(m f^3). SCOPE: +-1 weights only, A fixed in advance (not adaptive), no bound on survivors in time beyond the poly count. Integer weights break Step 3 (Y is no longer binomial). CONSEQUENCE for G0012(i): time poly(m,f) is below 2^k times the bound mk/sqrt(f) whenever 2^k >= C m f^3, i.e. k >= c log(mf). It does NOT yet give G0012(ii) or (iii), and does not cover adaptive A (G0016). This supersedes the S0031 review record marked REFUTED: the claim 'poly-time deterministic z*' is TRUE for +-1 weights, because conditional sums reduce to binomial convolutions, not to 2^f enumeration. The earlier claim that no poly-time method exists was wrong.
